title: Finite closed kernel adjoint agrees with the transported etale exceptional functor
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the coefficient categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $T=X,Z,U$.
Fix $n\ge1$ and $A=A_n$. Let $i^\times_{\rm et}$ be the right adjoint of the ordinary etale compact-support functor attached to the compactification $Z\xrightarrow1Z\xrightarrow iX$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let $J_n$ be the ambient pro-etale kernel adjoint of [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\rm proet}\to T_{\rm et}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The etale adjoint preserves bounded constructibility and has the supported triangle with the etale exceptional counit and open unit. On $D^b_c(X,A)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$J_nK\cong\nu_Z^*i^\times_{\rm et}R\nu_{X,*}K,$$
where the right-hand side is the transported finite exceptional inverse image formula of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For every bounded constructible etale origin $K\cong\nu_X^*K'$, the induced isomorphism between the two supported triangles is the unique one with the canonical middle and open components; it preserves the counit and consequently the adjunction unit. This normalization is independent of the chosen origin and compatible with shifts and with the canonical counit-transpose finite coefficient quotient comparisons: for $m\ge n$ and every $K\in D^b_c(X,A_m)$ whose derived reduction $K\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ lies in $D^b_c(X,A_n)$ (for instance a reduction $K_m$ of an integral constructible complex), the kernel-adjoint comparison $J_mK\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to J_n(K\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n)$, defined as the transpose of the coefficient-extended kernel counit, corresponds under the two finite isomorphisms to the site-comparison image of the etale counit-transpose quotient comparison; no flatness of $A_m\to A_n$ is assumed. In particular it identifies the coefficient-system realization of the specified exceptional functor, not just an unnamed right adjoint. For integral $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ let $J_R$ be the right adjoint of $i_*$ over the completed coefficient sheaves, constructed by [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint] using $i^{-1}B_X\cong B_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. If $J_RK$ is integral constructible and its counit-normalized reductions are $J_nK_n$ compatibly with quotient transitions, the induced isomorphism of its normalized reduction tower with that specified exceptional coefficient tower gives the natural identification
$$J_RK\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(Ri_n^!K_n)=Ri_R^!K$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z))$, preserving the exceptional counit and units; here $B_Z=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_Z$ and the right limit is taken on the actual derived coefficient system of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

proof.text: The specified compactification $(1_Z,i)$ identifies ordinary etale compact support with exact termwise $i_*$, with its actual derived comparison, by lem-pur-closed-unbounded-compact-support-normalization. Transport the etale support adjunction along this isomorphism: det-sp-unique-right-adjoint identifies $i^\times_{\rm et}$ with the support right adjoint, carrying the counit. Hence lem-exc-closed-support-triangle supplies its triangle with the etale exceptional counit and open unit. Choose a finite dimension bound $d$ for $X$ by lem-kun-dimension-finite-type; if $X$ is empty choose $d=0$. The open complement is quasi-compact since $X$ is Noetherian. The prime-to-characteristic finite ring $A_n$ satisfies lem-exc-open-complement-known with $c=2d$. Applying lem-exc-closed-amplitude proves bounded constructible preservation of the etale adjoint, without a finite-Tor assumption.

source.place: Finite stage: comparison of the supported triangles and the specified functor

proof.text: For any ambient $P,N$ and any integer $a$, the adjunctions and $j^*i_*=0$ of lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint give $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[a],Rj_*N)=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*i_*P[a],N)=0$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-triangle-morphism-extension to the two support triangles with their canonical middle and open components. Its orthogonality hypothesis is exactly this vanishing, so their triangle isomorphism is unique, including the boundary arrow. Equivalently its closed component is the adjunction transpose of the same counit. This characterizes the comparison without a choice of origin. Naturality in $K$, independence of the origin, and cocycles for changing origins follow because both composites have the same counit transpose. Counit-compatible uniqueness also carries the units: the adjoint of $1_{i_*P}$ is the unit in either presentation. For shifts use the unique adjoint shift structure of lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique. For a quotient $A_m\to A_n$ and an input $K$ as in the statement, write $T=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$. The pro-etale closed projection $q:T(i_*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*(TP)$ is invertible by lem-weil-proetale-closed-tensor-projection (ring $(A_m)_X$, second argument $(A_n)_X$, with $i^{-1}(A_n)_X=(A_n)_Z$); its coefficient-adjunction transpose is $i_*$ of the scalar unit. Define the kernel-adjoint comparison by transposing $T(\varepsilon_m)\circ q^{-1}$ under $i_*\dashv J_n$; the corresponding etale comparison is the counit transpose in lem-pur-etale-system-quotient-normalization. Under the site tensor and direct-image identifications the two transposes agree: the finite isomorphisms preserve the counits, and $q$ agrees with $\nu^*$ of the etale projection since both are the transposes of $i_*$ of the scalar unit. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection makes the quotient squares commute; the same argument gives successive-quotient cocycles. This uses the actual quotient mates and does not assume quotient flatness.

source.place: Finite stage: uniqueness, origin independence, shifts and quotient normalization

proof.text:
For the conditional integral assertion put $C=\mathcal R_XK$ and $M=\mathcal R_Z(J_RK)$ in the actual derived categories of strict varying-coefficient systems of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image. Reducing the integral counit is an actual system map $\mathcal R_X(i_*J_RK)	o C$. Precompose with $r_{J_RK}^{-1}$ of lem-sf-closed-direct-image-strict-reduction to obtain $a:i_{*, ullet}M	o C$. The hypothesis on counit-normalized reductions says that its evaluations are the kernel counits after the given identifications $M_n\cong J_nK_n$. Both $C$ and $M$ are bounded below systems of etale origin: integral constructibility gives a common cohomological interval, and finite-ring constructible origin gives origin levelwise. By lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison their comparison counits are invertible. Apply $R
u_{X, ullet,*}$ to $a$ and identify $R
u_{X, ullet,*}i_{*, ullet}\cong i_{*, ullet}^{m et}R
u_{Z, ullet,*}$ by derived pushforward composition, applied to the small diagram sites of systems. Transpose this actual map under $i_{*, ullet}^{m et}\dashv G_{i,A}$ of lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint, then pull it back by $
u_{Z, ullet}^*$. This constructs a natural map $b:M	o\mathcal T_iK$, where $\mathcal T_iK=
u_{Z, ullet}^*G_{i,A}R
u_{X, ullet,*}C$ is exactly the specified system in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image. Evaluation respects both adjunctions and their counits by the two system lemmas; hence $e_nb$ is exactly the counit-preserving finite isomorphism already proved. In particular $b$ is invertible: its cone has zero cohomology at every level, and cohomology of strict coefficient systems is levelwise. This constructs the map before evaluation; it does not assert faithfulness or uniqueness of lifts of levelwise derived maps.

source.place: Integral stage: construct the actual system isomorphism by transposing the reduced counit

proof.text: Apply the exact functor $R\lim\circ DU_Z$ to $b$. The output on $\mathcal T_iK$ is literally $Ri_R^!K$ by def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image. On $M$ the canonical quotient augmentation $J_RK\to R\lim DU_ZM$ is invertible: $J_RK$ is integral constructible by hypothesis and lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence identifies its Roos completeness with invertibility of this specified augmentation. Its hypothesis that $(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi))$ is an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] holds: $\mathcal O_E$ is Noetherian, $\mathcal O_E/\varpi$ is a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and each $A_n$ is finite with the two-term free resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}\mathcal O_E]$, hence perfect. The composite gives the asserted natural integral identification. Its counit equation holds as an equation of systems before taking the limit, since $b$ was the adjunction transpose of $a$; the inverse site-comparison counits and the augmentation commute by naturality. Closed $i_*$ commutes with this derived limit: it is a right adjoint to exact $i^*$, so it preserves K-injective resolutions and the ordinary limit, yielding the derived comparison. Thus taking the limit of the system counit equation gives the integral counit equation. The unit equation follows by transposing the identity under the integral adjunction and its transported adjunction, just as in Step 3. This identifies the specified exceptional realization on morphisms as well as objects.
